description: What JPA and Hibernate read from a project's own Java besides the mapping annotations: which annotations the project declares cannot change how an attribute is mapped.

rules.description: An annotation on an entity attribute changes nothing about its column when the project declares it, its declaration carries only annotations from java.lang.annotation, and no class of the project implements a Hibernate boot extension point. Hibernate reads a project's own annotation only through a meta-annotation on its declaration or through code handed to it at boot, so the column keeps the grade its mapping gives it.
rules.why: ngrinder marks 27 PerfTest fields with its own @Cloneable (@Target, @Retention and @Documented only), and every one of those columns was graded a guess because the JPA lane did not know the name.

extensionPoints.source: hibernate-core 6.6 and 7.1, org/hibernate/integrator/spi/Integrator.java: integrate(Metadata, BootstrapContext, SessionFactoryImplementor) is handed the whole mapping
hibernate-core 6.6 and 7.1, org/hibernate/jpa/boot/spi/IntegratorProvider.java: hands Hibernate the Integrators above through hibernate.integrator_provider
hibernate-core 6.6 and 7.1, org/hibernate/boot/spi/AdditionalMappingContributor.java: contributes mappings at boot
hibernate-core 6.6 and 7.1, org/hibernate/boot/spi/MetadataBuilderFactory.java: builds the MetadataBuilder itself
spring-boot-autoconfigure 3.x, HibernatePropertiesCustomizer.java: customize(Map) sets any Hibernate property, an integrator provider among them

examples.why: ngrinder's marker: declared in the tree, java.lang.annotation only
a meta-annotation imported with its package, or written in full, is still java.lang.annotation's
a Hibernate meta-annotation makes Hibernate run the annotation's binder, which may change the column
an Integrator is handed the whole mapping at boot and may read any annotation
an Integrator the tree registers in a ServiceLoader file, perhaps a class from a jar: Hibernate loads it the same way
an annotation from a jar: its declaration is not in the tree
Target may be com.lib's, a package imported whole that the rule does not list

rules.description: Spring Boot builds the EntityManagerFactory itself and gives it its naming (CamelCaseToUnderscoresNamingStrategy, SpringImplicitNamingStrategy) unless the project defines one: then Boot backs off, and a factory the project builds by hand runs Hibernate's own naming (PhysicalNamingStrategyStandardImpl, which keeps a name as written, and ImplicitNamingStrategyJpaCompliantImpl, which names a default join table after the two tables). A factory built by hand is a `new` of one of factoryTypes or builderTypes, a Spring XML bean of one, or a @Bean method that returns one of factoryTypes and takes no builder. A @Bean method that takes one of builderTypes as a parameter and constructs no factory itself is built from Boot's builder, which carries Boot's naming from Spring Boot 3.4 on and only spring.jpa.properties before. A naming setting in code is a key of namingProperties put into a map by a class that declares @Bean methods, or set on a factory bean in XML (a <prop>, an <entry>, or a bean property of namingSetters); its value names a strategy when it states a class of strategyClasses. A type the file does not place among these is not a factory, and a setting whose value is not stated is said without a strategy.
rules.why: ngrinder builds its LocalContainerEntityManagerFactoryBean with new in DatabaseConfig and sets no naming, so Hibernate keeps @Column(name = "hostName") as hostName, as its DDL has it; the engine assumed Spring Boot's default and drew host_name. egov-msa-edu builds its factories from Boot's EntityManagerFactoryBuilder under Spring Boot 3.5, and its DDL has created_by: Boot's naming reaches a builder-made factory there.

factoryTypes.source: spring-orm 5.3.39 and 6.1.14 LocalContainerEntityManagerFactoryBean.java:90/89, in the 7.0.8 jar; Spring Boot backs off for it (JpaBaseConfiguration @ConditionalOnMissingBean, 2.7.18:130, 3.3.5:131, spring-boot-jpa 4.0.0:140)
spring-orm 5.3.39 LocalEntityManagerFactoryBean.java:62, 6.1.14:58, in the 7.0.8 jar: a FactoryBean of EntityManagerFactory, which Boot backs off for
spring-orm 5.3.39 and 6.1.14 AbstractEntityManagerFactoryBean.java:92: what a @Bean method may declare it returns
the type Boot's @ConditionalOnMissingBean names (Boot 3 and 4): a @Bean of it is the project's own factory
hibernate-core 6.6 SessionFactory.java:139 extends EntityManagerFactory, so a @Bean of it is an EntityManagerFactory bean
spring-orm 7.0.8 jar: the Hibernate factory bean moved out of orm.hibernate5
spring-orm 3.2.18 and 4.3.30 hibernate4/: Hibernate 4 runs EJB3NamingStrategy by default (hibernate-core 4.3.11 LegacyNamingStrategyDelegator.java:48-49), the same names as identity and JPA-compliant

builderTypes.source: spring-boot 2.7.18 and 3.3.5 EntityManagerFactoryBuilder.java; its map goes into the factory (3.3.5:258). Auto-configured with spring.jpa.properties only up to 3.3 (JpaBaseConfiguration 2.7.18:122-123, 3.3.13:123-124) and with Boot's vendor properties, naming included, from 3.4.0 (:123-135)
spring-boot-jpa 4.0.0 EntityManagerFactoryBuilder.java; auto-configured with the vendor properties (JpaBaseConfiguration.java:124-136)

namingProperties.source: hibernate-core 6.6 MappingSettings.java:381, 7.1:405; AvailableSettings extends MappingSettings (6.6:31-34) and Environment implements AvailableSettings (6.6:134, 7.1:133)

namingSetters.name: physicalNamingStrategy
namingSetters.source: spring-orm 6.1.14 hibernate5/LocalSessionFactoryBean.java:281 setPhysicalNamingStrategy, the bean property an XML <property> sets

strategyClasses.source: hibernate-core 6.6 and 7.1: the name as written; Hibernate's own default (MetadataBuilderImpl 6.6:737-741)
spring-boot 2.7.18 and 3.3.5: overrides only determineJoinTableName, the owning table and the attribute

hibernate-core 6.6 ImplicitNamingStrategyJpaCompliantImpl.java:64-74: a join table is the owning table and the other table; Hibernate's own default, also by the names default and jpa (StrategySelectorBuilder 6.6:232-242)

examples.why: ngrinder's DatabaseConfig: a @Bean that builds its factory with new, said once at the new
egov-msa-edu's board service: the factory is built from the builder Spring Boot hands out
a @Bean of the EntityManagerFactory type that takes no builder: Boot backs off for it, and its naming is not Boot's
a naming key put by a helper of the configuration class, with a class Hibernate ships as its value
the key written as Hibernate's constant and the value as a class's name, in a customizer a @Bean returns

examples.xml:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans">
  <bean id="entityManagerFactory" class="org.springframework.orm.jpa.LocalContainerEntityManagerFactoryBean">
    <property name="dataSource" ref="dataSource"/>
    <property name="jpaProperties">
      <props>
        <prop key="hibernate.physical_naming_strategy">egovframework.com.cmm.EgovNamingStrategy</prop>
      </props>
    </property>
  </bean>
</beans>
examples.why: the eGovFrame spelling: a factory bean in a Spring XML, with a naming class of the project's own, which names no strategy this engine models
a Hibernate session factory bean told its physical strategy through the bean property
a builder the project constructs itself carries only the properties it is given, not Boot's naming
a type of the same simple name from another package is not Spring's

rules.description: A Hibernate factory is told its naming strategy in code by a setter: setPhysicalNamingStrategy and setImplicitNamingStrategy on Spring's LocalSessionFactoryBean and LocalSessionFactoryBuilder and on Hibernate's Configuration, applyPhysicalNamingStrategy and applyImplicitNamingStrategy on Hibernate's MetadataBuilder, and setNamingStrategy on the Hibernate 3 and 4 factory beans. The strategy object is an argument this engine does not read, so the names it derives rest on an assumed strategy, and the profile's jpa.namingStrategy is where a project says which it is. A call is this setting when its receiver is declared as a type that declares the method, or as a type of the tree that extends one.
rules.why: A factory the project builds by hand does not take Spring Boot's naming, and one that is given its strategy by a setter names its tables by that strategy. Before this rule nothing said so.

params.effect: the factory it is called on names tables and columns by the strategy it is given, and the names this pack derives rest on an assumed one

calls.why: spring-orm 6.1.14 hibernate5/LocalSessionFactoryBean.java:281; the 7.0.8 class in orm.jpa.hibernate declares it too
inherited from org.hibernate.cfg.Configuration (hibernate-core 6.6 Configuration.java:366), named here because the builder is the type a project declares
spring-orm 4.3.30 hibernate3/LocalSessionFactoryBean.java:400 and hibernate4/LocalSessionFactoryBean.java:226: Hibernate 3 and 4's one naming strategy

examples.why: Spring's Hibernate factory bean told its physical strategy, on a local declared as the bean
the builder inherits the setter from Hibernate's Configuration; the method is listed under both
Hibernate's own bootstrap API
a project's own setter with the name, on its own type, is not Hibernate's
